tasks.title: Define Heartbeat consumer contracts, copied configuration and weak registration ownership
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: AC-1/AC-4/AC-7: provide the two-method consumer registration API and awaited subscriber contract; snapshot10ms/default-zero schedule and validate documented duration/name limits; resolve MaxConcurrent once with invariant environment/setup/default precedence and1..16 range. Preserve actual EnvironmentOptions architecture. Define one actual owner with a weak idle association and atomic lifetime-hold contract used by the engine; no alternate scheduler, subscriber disposal transfer or generic startup framework. Include meaningful configuration/identity/reference-graph tests and independent review.
tasks.validation: Build affected Core/test projects, run the focused new Heartbeat configuration/contract tests plus affected EnvironmentOptions architecture/constructor assertions. Inspect public XML contract and bound-condition/owner graphs. Record actual native results and applicable source AT coverage; preserve old module defaults and dependency closure. No release qualification claim.

tasks.title: Implement monotonic fair Heartbeat scheduling and exclusive asynchronous execution
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: AC-1/AC-2: one application engine uses reference identity/CWT bindings, weak idle entries and a single monotonic timer; at most one accepted execution per registration and MaxConcurrent unfinished dispatched wrappers. FIFO ready work progresses one released slot at a time. Conditions, callback, awaited exception-only OnError, cleanup and reporting retain exclusivity and owner holds; full settlement starts the fixed delay. Register never invokes subscriber code inline; duplicate settings stay unchanged. Include controlled time/executor/capacity/outcome tests, docs and review.
tasks.validation: Build the affected native projects and run Heartbeat timing, identity, duplicate-race, non-overlap, fairness, bounded-state, synchronous-prologue and result/error tests using ManualTimeProvider and controlled tasks. Verify no user code or arbitrary owner/reporting callback under scheduler lock, no per-idle-registration task history, no business timeout/retry/health arithmetic.

tasks.title: Complete Heartbeat cutoffs, retirement and true owner settlement barriers
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: AC-3/AC-4: unregister/owner close drain accepted queued/running work; global cutoff additionally suppresses condition/callback phases that have not won their start gate. Await posted wrappers, handlers, owned cleanup and reporting before barrier completion, with caller-only wait cancellation and no automatic execution cancellation. Retain identity until true drain, support sequential reuse, safely retire collected/unusable targets and report once through an independently retained safe Core binding. Detect direct own-barrier waits. Include deterministic boundary/race/reachability checks and review.
tasks.validation: Run focused native tests with blocked phases, paused wrappers, already-canceled waits, concurrent stop/unregister, owner-close/admission races, cleanup/reporting faults and full target/condition/owner/exception graph GC. Assert no callback after losing a start gate, no early owner/slot release and exactly-once collection retirement while an external monitor survives.

tasks.title: Extend detached Healthcheck facts and implement Heartbeat policy binding
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: AC-5/AC-7: append Dispatched/Suppressed facts and optional raw boolean/cancellation/timing context without changing existing enum values, outcomes or phase strings. Merge immutable bounded context, retain neutral suppression without policy arithmetic, preserve cleanup-error precedence in one final Outcome and distinct settlement. Select existing monitor/consecutive-failure/availability bindings once, isolate reporting failures, preserve external/created-monitor ownership and old reports. Keep live configuration in target-dependent graph and safe concrete binder available for collection retirement. Include affected receiving/wire/compatibility tests, docs and independent review.
tasks.validation: Build and run focused existing/new native Healthcheck binder, fact validation, snapshot, formatter/protocol and compatibility cases for dispatch/suppression/result context, duplicates, contradictions and optional legacy payloads. New Healthcheck tests can run before engine binding integration; complete real adapter tests with engine before task completion. No forced old baseline rewrite or invented durable delivery guarantee.

tasks.title: Integrate Heartbeat readiness, safe DI scope shutdown and developer package example
tasks.acceptanceCriteria: AC-6/AC-7: provide a narrow application-owned Generic Host adapter and actual owner-bound scope wrapper: ready dependencies precede activation, no ApplicationStarted self-deadlock, both stopping paths close starts, actual drain precedes dependent stopping and scope/root disposal even after canceled waits. Deliver hosted polling example from source and exact development package in ordinary build/folder publish; include false/exception/refresh/stop observations, concise usage, native host/business/package checks and integrated independent review. Preserve existing module behavior and all historical owners/evidence. Settle actual current accounting; leave all unexecuted platform and release obligations explicit.
tasks.validation: Run real local Windows host/scope/business tests covering readiness, early stop, running-condition/callback/error handling and dependency disposal ordering. Build and consume the current development package in the Heartbeat example, including folder publish and executable shutdown. Run meaningful affected architecture/compatibility regression only after source stabilizes. Record all AT mappings and actual evidence, review scope/complexity and verify resources settled. No Ubuntu/release/coverage/mutation/performance claim without actual separately authorized work.
